cold_open.hook: Nasdaq up 0.80%, but Eli Lilly just tanked 2.96%—the AI boom's favorite pharma play is suddenly looking mortal.

markets.macro_note: Tech rallying on AI optimism while biotech stumbles; VIX compression signals complacency.

big_story.story_title: The New (And Slightly Smelly) Center of the AI Boom
big_story.angle: Where is the actual AI infrastructure being built, and why are the real estate and logistics costs turning out to be the unglamorous bottleneck nobody wants to talk about?

quick_hits.angle: NVIDIA and Palantir's government AI partnership is the real moat—not consumer chatbots, but the infrastructure states and defense contractors will actually pay for.
Trump's defense budget is massive, but the U.S. war machine is depleted—states are now bidding against each other for manufacturing contracts, turning national security into a jobs program.
Proton's privacy-focused AI chatbot is the contrarian play—while everyone else chases scale, they're betting on the user who actually cares if their prompts get logged.
Palantir stock crashed but the fundamentals (government contracts, AI deployment) are real—this is the dip that separates hype traders from actual conviction holders.

odd_thing.joke_angle: DC's new cinematic universe started hot and is already slowing down—turns out you can't just throw money at IP and expect it to stick when the actual stories are mid.

yesterday_callback.topic: Supreme Court nukes FTC independence—commissioners can now be fired at will, handing tech regulation back to whoever controls the executive
yesterday_callback.fresh_take: Today's NVIDIA-Palantir government AI deal is the direct consequence: with FTC toothless, the real power consolidates around defense contracts and state partnerships instead of consumer protection.

sign_off.callback_target: Palantir—the stock that crashed but the government contracts that didn't.
